# 1 Kings Chapter 8 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Then Solomon assembled the elders of Israel and all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the fathers' houses of the people of Israel, before King Solomon in Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of the City of David, which is Zion.
**2** And all the men of Israel assembled to King Solomon at the feast in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
**3** And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.
**4** And they brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites brought them up.
**5** And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, who had assembled before him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
**6** Then the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the LORD to its place in the inner sanctuary of the house, in the Most Holy Place, underneath the wings of the cherubim.
**7** For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim overshadowed the ark and its poles from above.
**8** And the poles were so long that the ends of the poles were seen from the Holy Place before the inner sanctuary, but they could not be seen from outside. And they are there to this day.
**9** There was nothing in the ark except the two tablets of stone that Moses had placed there at Horeb, where the LORD made a covenant with the people of Israel, when they came out of the land of Egypt.
**10** And when the priests came out of the Holy Place, a cloud filled the house of the LORD,
**11** so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
**12** Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
**13** I have indeed built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell in forever."
**14** Then the king turned his face about and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood.
**15** And he said, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who with his mouth spoke to David my father and with his hand has fulfilled it, saying,
**16** 'Since the day that I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, that my name might be there. But I chose David to be over my people Israel.'
**17** Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
**18** But the LORD said to David my father, 'Whereas it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.
**19** Nevertheless, you shall not build the house, but your son who shall come from your body, he shall build the house for my name.'
**20** Now the LORD has fulfilled his word that he spoke. For I have risen in the place of David my father, and I sit on the throne of Israel, as the LORD promised, and I have built the house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
**21** And there I have provided a place for the ark, in which is the covenant of the LORD that he made with our fathers, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt."
**22** Then Solomon stood before the altar of the LORD in the presence of all the assembly of Israel and spread out his hands toward heaven,
**23** and said, "O LORD, God of Israel, there is no God like you, in heaven above or on earth beneath, keeping covenant and showing steadfast love to your servants who walk before you with all their heart,
**24** who have kept with your servant David my father what you declared to him. You spoke with your mouth, and with your hand have fulfilled it this day.
**25** Now therefore, O LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you promised him, saying, 'You shall not lack a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons pay close attention to their way, to walk before me as you have walked before me.'
**26** Now therefore, O God of Israel, let your word be confirmed, which you spoke to your servant David my father.
**27** But will God indeed dwell on the earth? Behold, heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you; how much less this house that I have built!
**28** Yet have regard to the prayer of your servant and to his plea, O LORD my God, listening to the cry and to the prayer that your servant prays before you this day,
**29** that your eyes may be open night and day toward this house, the place of which you have said, 'My name shall be there,' that you may listen to the prayer that your servant offers toward this place.
**30** And listen to the plea of your servant and of your people Israel, when they pray toward this place. And listen in heaven your dwelling place, and when you hear, forgive.
**31** If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath and comes and swears his oath before your altar in this house,
**32** then hear in heaven and act and judge your servants, condemning the guilty by bringing his conduct on his own head, and vindicating the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
**33** When your people Israel are defeated before the enemy because they have sinned against you, and if they turn again to you and acknowledge your name and pray and plead with you in this house,
**34** then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your people Israel and bring them again to the land that you gave to their fathers.
**35** When heaven is shut up and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, if they pray toward this place and acknowledge your name and turn from their sin, when you afflict them,
**36** then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk, and grant rain upon your land that you have given to your people as an inheritance.
**37** If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence or blight or mildew or locust or caterpillar, if their enemy besieges them in the land at their gates, whatever plague, whatever sickness there is,
**38** whatever prayer, whatever plea is made by any man or by all your people Israel, each knowing the affliction of his own heart and stretching out his hands toward this house,
**39** then hear in heaven your dwelling place and forgive and act and render to each whose heart you know, according to all his ways — for you, you only, know the hearts of all the children of mankind —
**40** that they may fear you all the days that they live in the land that you gave to our fathers.
**41** Likewise, when a foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, comes from a far country for your name's sake —
**42** for they shall hear of your great name and your mighty hand and of your outstretched arm — when he comes and prays toward this house,
**43** hear in heaven your dwelling place and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to you, in order that all peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your people Israel, and that they may know that this house that I have built is called by your name.
**44** If your people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatever way you shall send them, and they pray to the LORD toward the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
**45** then hear in heaven their prayer and their plea, and maintain their cause.
**46** If they sin against you — for there is no man who does not sin — and you are angry with them and give them to an enemy, so that they are carried away captive to the land of the enemy, far off or near,
**47** yet if they turn their heart in the land to which they have been carried captive, and repent and plead with you in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned and have acted perversely and wickedly,'
**48** if they repent with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies who carried them captive, and pray to you toward their land, which you gave to their fathers, the city that you have chosen, and the house that I have built for your name,
**49** then hear in heaven your dwelling place their prayer and their plea, and maintain their cause
**50** and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all their transgressions that they have committed against you, and grant them compassion in the sight of those who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them.
**51** For they are your people and your heritage, which you brought out of Egypt, from the midst of the iron furnace.
**52** Let your eyes be open to the plea of your servant and to the plea of your people Israel, giving ear to them whenever they call to you.
**53** For you separated them from among all the peoples of the earth to be your heritage, as you declared through Moses your servant, when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord GOD."
**54** Now when Solomon finished offering all this prayer and plea to the LORD, he arose from before the altar of the LORD, where he had knelt with his hands spread out toward heaven.
**55** And he stood and blessed all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying,
**56** "Blessed be the LORD who has given rest to his people Israel, according to all that he promised. Not one word has failed of all his good promise, which he spoke through Moses his servant.
**57** The LORD our God be with us, as he was with our fathers. May he not leave us or forsake us,
**58** that he may incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his rules, which he commanded our fathers.
**59** Let these words of mine, with which I have pleaded before the LORD, be near to the LORD our God day and night, and may he maintain the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel, as each day requires,
**60** that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God; there is no other.
**61** Let your heart therefore be wholly true to the LORD our God, walking in his statutes and keeping his commandments, as at this day."
**62** Then the king, and all Israel with him, offered sacrifice before the LORD.
**63** Solomon offered as peace offerings to the LORD twenty-two thousand oxen and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people of Israel dedicated the house of the LORD.
**64** The same day the king consecrated the middle of the court that was before the house of the LORD, for there he offered the burnt offerings and the grain offerings and the fat pieces of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that was before the LORD was too small to receive the burnt offerings and the grain offerings and the fat pieces of the peace offerings.
**65** So Solomon held the feast at that time, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from Lebo-hamath to the Brook of Egypt, before the LORD our God, seven days and seven days, fourteen days.
**66** On the eighth day he sent the people away, and they blessed the king and went to their homes joyful and glad of heart for all the goodness that the LORD had shown to David his servant and to Israel his people.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA has reviewed the translations of EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), and PNEUMA (dynamic) for this chapter.

**Method**: Each verse was compared across all three translations. The LOGOS formal translation serves as the primary consensus baseline, with adjustments where EMET's literalism reveals important Hebrew features or PNEUMA's dynamic rendering better captures the original intent.

**Key Observations**:
- EMET preserves Hebrew word order and particles (ʾet, vav-consecutive) that reveal syntactic emphasis
- LOGOS provides the most balanced English rendering suitable for study
- PNEUMA's dynamic approach often captures emotional register and narrative pacing most effectively

## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

**Chapter 8**: 35 verse(s) with significant divergence

### Verse 2
- **EMET**: And-all the-men-of Israel assembled to the-king Solomon at-the-feast, in-the-month-of Ethanim — it is the-seventh month.
- **LOGOS**: And all the men of Israel assembled to King Solomon at the feast in the month of Ethanim, which is the seventh month.
- **PNEUMA**: All the men of Israel came together before King Solomon during the festival in the month of Ethanim, the seventh month.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 3
- **EMET**: And-all the-elders-of Israel came, and-the-priests took-up ʾet-the-ark.
- **LOGOS**: And all the elders of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark.
- **PNEUMA**: When all the elders arrived, the priests took up the ark
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 4
- **EMET**: And-they-brought-up ʾet-the-ark-of YHWH, and-ʾet-the-tent-of meeting, and-ʾet-all the-holy vessels that were in-the-tent. And-the-priests and-the-Levites brought-them-up.
- **LOGOS**: And they brought up the ark of the LORD, the tent of meeting, and all the holy vessels that were in the tent. The priests and the Levites brought them up.
- **PNEUMA**: and brought it up, along with the tent of meeting and all its sacred furnishings. The priests and Levites carried them.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 5
- **EMET**: And-the-king Solomon and-all the-congregation-of Israel who-assembled to-him were with-him before the-ark, sacrificing sheep and-cattle that could-not be-numbered or-counted from-multitude.
- **LOGOS**: And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, who had assembled before him, were with him before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and oxen that they could not be counted or numbered.
- **PNEUMA**: King Solomon and the entire congregation of Israel gathered before the ark, sacrificing so many sheep and cattle that no one could keep count.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 7
- **EMET**: For the-cherubim spread wings to the-place-of the-ark, and-the-cherubim covered over the-ark and-over its-poles from-above.
- **LOGOS**: For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, so that the cherubim overshadowed the ark and its poles from above.
- **PNEUMA**: The cherubim's wings spread over the place where the ark rested, sheltering the ark and its carrying poles from above.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 11
- **EMET**: And-the-priests could-not stand to-minister because-of the-cloud, for the-glory-of YHWH filled ʾet-the-house-of YHWH.
- **LOGOS**: so that the priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD.
- **PNEUMA**: The priests could not continue ministering because of the cloud — the glory of the LORD had filled the temple.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 12
- **EMET**: Then Solomon said, "YHWH said he-would-dwell in-the-thick-darkness.
- **LOGOS**: Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said that he would dwell in thick darkness.
- **PNEUMA**: Then Solomon said, "The LORD has said he would live in a dark cloud.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 13
- **EMET**: I-have-surely-built a-house-of exaltation for-you, a-place for-your-dwelling forever."
- **LOGOS**: I have indeed built you an exalted house, a place for you to dwell in forever."
- **PNEUMA**: I have built a magnificent temple for you — a place for you to live forever."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 14
- **EMET**: And-the-king turned ʾet-his-face and-blessed ʾet-all the-assembly-of Israel, and-all the-assembly-of Israel was-standing.
- **LOGOS**: Then the king turned his face about and blessed all the assembly of Israel, while all the assembly of Israel stood.
- **PNEUMA**: The king turned to face the whole assembly of Israel, who were standing, and he blessed them.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 16
- **EMET**: 'From the-day that I-brought-out ʾet-my-people ʾet-Israel from-Egypt, I-did-not choose a-city from-all the-tribes-of Israel to-build a-house for-my-name to-be there. But-I-chose David to-be over my-pe...
- **LOGOS**: 'Since the day that I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel in which to build a house, that my name might be there. But I chose David to be over my peo...
- **PNEUMA**: He said, 'From the day I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I have never chosen a city in any tribe of Israel for a temple to be built for my name. But I chose David to rule my people Israel.'
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 17
- **EMET**: And-it-was with the-heart-of David my-father to-build a-house for-the-name-of YHWH, the-God-of Israel.
- **LOGOS**: Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
- **PNEUMA**: My father David set his heart on building a temple for the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 18
- **EMET**: And-YHWH said to David my-father, 'Because it-was with your-heart to-build a-house for-my-name, you-did-well that it-was with your-heart.
- **LOGOS**: But the LORD said to David my father, 'Whereas it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart.
- **PNEUMA**: But the LORD told my father David, 'It is good that you wanted to build a temple for my name.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 19
- **EMET**: Only, you shall-not build the-house; but your-son who-comes-out from-your-loins — he will-build the-house for-my-name.'
- **LOGOS**: Nevertheless, you shall not build the house, but your son who shall come from your body, he shall build the house for my name.'
- **PNEUMA**: But you are not the one who will build it. Your own son — he will build the temple for my name.'
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 24
- **EMET**: who kept for-your-servant David my-father ʾet-what you-spoke to-him. And-you-spoke with-your-mouth, and-with-your-hand you-fulfilled, as-this day.
- **LOGOS**: who have kept with your servant David my father what you declared to him. You spoke with your mouth, and with your hand have fulfilled it this day.
- **PNEUMA**: You have kept the promise you made to your servant, my father David. With your own mouth you promised it, and with your own hand you have fulfilled it today.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 25
- **EMET**: And-now, YHWH, God-of Israel, keep for-your-servant David my-father ʾet-what you-spoke to-him, saying, 'There-shall-not be-cut-off for-you a-man from-before-me sitting on the-throne-of Israel — only i...
- **LOGOS**: Now therefore, O LORD, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you promised him, saying, 'You shall not lack a man to sit before me on the throne of Israel, if only your sons pay clo...
- **PNEUMA**: Now, LORD God of Israel, keep the other promise you made to my father David: 'You will always have a descendant sitting on the throne of Israel — if your sons are careful to walk before me as you have...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 26
- **EMET**: And-now, God-of Israel, let-your-word be-confirmed, please, that you-spoke to your-servant David my-father.
- **LOGOS**: Now therefore, O God of Israel, let your word be confirmed, which you spoke to your servant David my father.
- **PNEUMA**: God of Israel, please confirm the word you spoke to your servant David.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 28
- **EMET**: And-turn to the-prayer-of your-servant and-to his-plea, YHWH my-God, to-hear the-cry and-the-prayer that your-servant prays before-you today —
- **LOGOS**: Yet have regard to the prayer of your servant and to his plea, O LORD my God, listening to the cry and to the prayer that your servant prays before you this day,
- **PNEUMA**: Yet, LORD my God, hear the prayer and the plea your servant is making before you today.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 31
- **EMET**: When a-man sins against his-neighbor, and-an-oath is-laid upon-him to-make-him-swear, and-he-comes and-swears before your-altar in-this house —
- **LOGOS**: If a man sins against his neighbor and is made to take an oath and comes and swears his oath before your altar in this house,
- **PNEUMA**: When someone wrongs another person and is required to take an oath, and they come and swear before your altar in this temple —
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 32
- **EMET**: then you, hear in-the-heavens, and-act, and-judge ʾet-your-servants, condemning the-guilty, to-bring his-way upon his-head, and-justifying the-righteous, to-give to-him according-to his-righteousness.
- **LOGOS**: then hear in heaven and act and judge your servants, condemning the guilty by bringing his conduct on his own head, and vindicating the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.
- **PNEUMA**: hear from heaven and act. Judge between your servants: condemn the guilty and bring their actions down on their own heads, and vindicate the innocent by treating them as their innocence deserves.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 36
- **EMET**: then you, hear in-the-heavens, and-forgive the-sin-of your-servants and-your-people Israel — for you-teach-them the-good way in-which they-should-walk — and-give rain upon your-land that you-gave to-y...
- **LOGOS**: then hear in heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk, and grant rain upon your land that you have given to your peop...
- **PNEUMA**: hear from heaven and forgive the sin of your servants, your people Israel. Teach them the right way to live, and send rain on the land you gave your people as their inheritance.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 37
- **EMET**: Famine when-it-is in-the-land, pestilence when-it-is, blight, mildew, locust, caterpillar when-it-is; when his-enemy besieges-him in-the-land-of his-gates — any plague, any sickness —
- **LOGOS**: If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence or blight or mildew or locust or caterpillar, if their enemy besieges them in the land at their gates, whatever plague, whatever sickness there i...
- **PNEUMA**: When famine or plague strikes the land, or blight or mildew, locusts or caterpillars — or when an enemy besieges any of their cities — whatever disaster or disease comes —
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 38
- **EMET**: any prayer, any plea that belongs-to any man, to-all your-people Israel, who knows each-one the-plague-of his-own-heart and-spreads-out his-palms toward this house —
- **LOGOS**: whatever prayer, whatever plea is made by any man or by all your people Israel, each knowing the affliction of his own heart and stretching out his hands toward this house,
- **PNEUMA**: when any prayer or plea is made by anyone among your people Israel, each one aware of their own suffering and spreading their hands toward this temple —
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 39
- **EMET**: then you, hear in-the-heavens, the-place-of your-dwelling, and-forgive, and-act, and-give to-each-man according-to all his-ways, whose heart you-know — for you alone know ʾet-the-heart-of all the-sons...
- **LOGOS**: then hear in heaven your dwelling place and forgive and act and render to each whose heart you know, according to all his ways — for you, you only, know the hearts of all the children of mankind —
- **PNEUMA**: hear from heaven, your dwelling place. Forgive and respond. Deal with each person according to all their ways, since you know their heart — for you alone know every human heart —
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 41
- **EMET**: And-also to the-foreigner who is not from-your-people Israel, and-he-comes from-a-far land for-the-sake-of your-name —
- **LOGOS**: Likewise, when a foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, comes from a far country for your name's sake —
- **PNEUMA**: And when a foreigner — someone who is not one of your people Israel — comes from a distant land because of your reputation,
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 42
- **EMET**: for they-will-hear ʾet-your-great name and-ʾet-your-strong hand and-your-outstretched arm — and-he-comes and-prays toward this house —
- **LOGOS**: for they shall hear of your great name and your mighty hand and of your outstretched arm — when he comes and prays toward this house,
- **PNEUMA**: because they have heard about your great name, your mighty power, and your outstretched arm — when they come and pray facing this temple,
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 43
- **EMET**: you, hear in-the-heavens, the-place-of your-dwelling, and-do according-to all that the-foreigner calls to-you, so-that all the-peoples-of the-earth may-know ʾet-your-name, to-fear you like your-people...
- **LOGOS**: hear in heaven your dwelling place and do according to all for which the foreigner calls to you, in order that all peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your people Israel, and t...
- **PNEUMA**: hear from heaven, your dwelling place, and do whatever the foreigner asks of you. Do this so that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and reverence you, just as your people Israel do, and ...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 44
- **EMET**: When your-people go-out to-battle against their-enemy, in-the-way that you-send-them, and-they-pray to YHWH toward the-city that you-chose and-the-house that I-built for-your-name —
- **LOGOS**: If your people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatever way you shall send them, and they pray to the LORD toward the city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
- **PNEUMA**: When your people go to war against their enemies, wherever you send them, and they pray to the LORD facing the city you have chosen and the temple I have built for your name —
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 46
- **EMET**: When they-sin against-you — for there-is-no man who does-not sin — and-you-are-angry with-them and-give-them before an-enemy, and-their-captors take-them-captive to the-land-of the-enemy, far or near,
- **LOGOS**: If they sin against you — for there is no man who does not sin — and you are angry with them and give them to an enemy, so that they are carried away captive to the land of the enemy, far off or near,
- **PNEUMA**: When they sin against you — and there is no one who does not sin — and you become angry with them and hand them over to their enemies, who carry them away as captives to their own land, whether far or...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 47
- **EMET**: and-they-take-it-to-heart in-the-land where they-were-taken-captive, and-they-return and-plead-for-grace to-you in-the-land-of their-captors, saying, 'We-have-sinned and-acted-perversely; we-have-done...
- **LOGOS**: yet if they turn their heart in the land to which they have been carried captive, and repent and plead with you in the land of their captors, saying, 'We have sinned and have acted perversely and wick...
- **PNEUMA**: and when they come to their senses in the land of their exile and repent and plead with you, saying, 'We have sinned; we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly' —
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 50
- **EMET**: and-forgive your-people who sinned against-you, and-all their-transgressions that they-transgressed against-you, and-give-them compassion before their-captors, and-they-will-have-compassion on-them.
- **LOGOS**: and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all their transgressions that they have committed against you, and grant them compassion in the sight of those who carried them captive, that t...
- **PNEUMA**: Forgive your people who have sinned against you. Forgive all their offenses against you. Cause their captors to show them mercy,
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 58
- **EMET**: to-incline our-hearts to-him, to-walk in-all his-ways, and-to-keep his-commandments and-his-statutes and-his-judgments that he-commanded ʾet-our-fathers.
- **LOGOS**: that he may incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his rules, which he commanded our fathers.
- **PNEUMA**: May he turn our hearts toward him, so that we walk in all his ways and keep the commands, laws, and rules he gave our ancestors.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.
